ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on the Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 18619, as amended; Arts. 2, 5, 7, 8, 12 and Enforcement Decree); Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality (Act No. 18951, as amended; Arts. 4, 5); Commercial Act (Act No. 12600, as amended; Arts. 237-287) and Commercial Registration Act; Personal Information Protection Act Art. 18(2); FATF Recommendations 10, 12 and 24 as implemented by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) guidance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Registration Matters (Certificate of Incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent court registry office under the Supreme Court of Korea (Commercial Registry, IROS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (MOFA); no consular legalization, as Korea is an Apostille Convention contracting state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Business Registration Certificate (Certificate of Good Standing for tax and VAT purposes)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service district tax office (Hometax)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by MOFA; no consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of the Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent court registry office or a Korean notary public (certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by Korean notary public followed by Hague Apostille by MOFA; no consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney appointing the incorporating counsel and bank signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All founding members of the Yuhan Hoesa, executed before a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by Korean notary public and Hague Apostille by MOFA; consular legalization is inapplicable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (corporate banking due diligence and financial standing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A Korean licensed commercial bank holding the pre-incorporation reserve account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the bank officer's signature and corporate seal by a Korean notary public, then Hague Apostille by MOFA; no consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding, counsel and the licensed financial institution shall conduct a three-tier screen: (i) PEP determination using FATF 40 Recommendation 12 and Korea-specific PEP list maintained by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit; (ii) automated sanctions search against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the US Department of the Treasury OFAC SDN and non-SDN 50% Rule lists, and the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; and (iii) adverse-media/litigation check on each director, signatory, and beneficial owner. The screen must re-run every 90 days and before each wire transfer, with negative hits escalated to KoFIU under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Commercial Registry Internet Service (IROS, www.iros.go.kr) with the National Tax Service Hometax business registration pre-check for licensed business scope
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Yuhan Hoesa must use a Korean-language trade name ending with the statutory suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' (limited liability company). Foreign-derived names must be rendered as a phonetic Hangul transliteration; an English or foreign script name may be recorded only as a supplementary transliterated trade name after registry approval. The four-tier naming doctrine requires (i) a personal or brand expression; (ii) a business purpose identifier; (iii) the statutory entity suffix; and (iv) a unique distinguishing element, so that no same-name or misleading resemblance exists in the same business purpose under the Commercial Act and Commercial Registration Rules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a written refusal identifying the conflicting or prohibited token. Within 14 days of receipt, the applicant may file an immediate appeal (immediate trial complaint) with the competent district court pursuant to the Korean Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, or may submit a corrected re-application on the IROS portal after removing or replacing the rejected token. The 30-day reservation cannot be extended. The appeal must attach the rejection notice, revised draft articles, and a certified name-search record; a new reservation must be secured before the incorporation filing is submitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for this industry. The National Tax Service requires an actual domestic place of business displaying a fixed door sign and functional facilities before issuing a value-added tax business registration certificate. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) and the airport operator require the in-flight catering kitchen to be physically located on or adjacent to the airport ramp side with controlled access. Korean banks refuse to accept a virtual office or mail-forwarding address for the corporate current account because the AML/CFT customer due diligence under KoFIU requires the company's physical address and CCTV/security arrangements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High, quantified at approximately 9 out of 10 in the first year of operation. Unannounced inspection checklist: (1) National Tax Service visit to verify actual place of business and bookkeeping within 60 days after registration; (2) municipal si-gun-gu food sanitation inspectors under the Food Sanitation Act checking HACCP, cold-chain logs, cooking and storage areas; (3) airport authority or civil aviation security auditors inspecting ramp vehicles, employee badges, and access control; (4) bank representative site visit as part of enhanced CDD for the catering license. Failure to pass any inspection results in administrative suspension or cancellation of the business registration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Local Tax Act; approximately KRW 120,000 for a zero-capital LLC plus 20% education surcharge.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee is prescribed for business registration certificate issuance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark under Korean Bar Association non-contentious corporate matters.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Korea Companies Act), Act No. 15986, Articles 287-2 through 287-22 (Yuhan Hoesa / Limited Liability Company); Article 542-2 (perpetual succession) and related registration provisions under the Court Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Company Registration Division, Civil Registry Department of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing through the Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of South Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Korean: Jeong-kwan) together with the Application for Company Registration (Hoesa Deungrok Shincheongseo) and supporting notarial deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa. The Articles must specify the authorized and subscribed capital. Before registration the full subscribed capital must be paid into a blocked deposit or escrow account at a licensed Korean bank, and a certificate of deposit must be presented to the court registry. Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, if foreign ownership is used, funds may remain in an escrow account until incorporation is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHANG HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY). This First Board Resolution (the Resolution) is made and adopted on the date set in the company register by the founding members and initial directors of YUHANG HOESA, a limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa) to be incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. All eligible directors and members have been given due notice, or have waived said notice, and a lawful quorum of the entire equity subscription is present. After deliberation, it is hereby RESOLVED as follows: (1) The Company shall be incorporated as a Yuhan Hoesa, a legal person distinct from its members, with its registered office at the address identified in the Articles of Incorporation. The registered office is adopted as the headquarters and principal place of business for all legal purposes. (2) The initial capital shall be the sum of KRW 200,000,000 divided into 200,000 ordinary shares, each with a par value of KRW 1,000, and all such shares have been subscribed by the founding members. The subscribed capital shall be paid up in full into a blocked corporate deposit account before registration, and the certificate of deposit shall be preserved as a statutory record. (3) The members and directors authorize the representative director and any authorized personnel to open one or more corporate bank accounts at domestic and international banks, to sign account mandate documents, and to instruct banks to disburse funds only according to resolutions of the Company. (4) The following statutory officers are appointed: the representative director of the Company, who shall have power to represent the Company with broad authority, and one auditor if required by the Articles, each of whom shall serve until removed or until successors are duly elected. (5) The directors are authorized to apply for the company registration and to take all further steps, including payment of fees, stamp taxes, and incidental expenses, to procure the legal existence and civil standing of the Company. (6) In view of the airline in-flight catering business, the directors are further authorized to obtain all food manufacturing licenses, airport ramp access permits, environmental clearances, fire safety certificates, and related government approvals, and to execute any agreement with the local airport operator. (7) The secretary is directed to record these resolutions in the corporate minute book and to deliver certified copies to Korean authorities upon request. This Resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Company Name Suitability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea (IRO) or the local District Court Registry in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At the Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea, the authorized formation agent will enter the proposed company name 'KR YUHANG HOESA' and business object codes corresponding to ISIC 5621 airline food manufacturing. The system will check identical or confusing names in the national corporate registry. Once the name is confirmed, submit a name reservation application through the court portal or in-person at the competent district court registry. The reservation remains valid for a limited statutory period, and any change to the intended business scope will require a fresh reservation.
required_dossiers: Passport or resident registration card of each founding member
Power of attorney for formation agent
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or title documents) if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is identical or confusingly similar to an existing Korean company, the court system will reject the reservation. The formation agent must immediately submit an alternate name, amend the draft Articles, and refile the same day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Notary Public under the Korean Ministry of Justice, acting within the territorial district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Korean notary public who is licensed by the Korean Ministry of Justice to review and acknowledge the Articles of Incorporation. The Articles must state the precise corporate purpose of operating an airline in-flight catering kitchen, the registered office address at a real physical location in the Republic of Korea, the names and identification numbers of all founding members, the share capital structure, the method of capital contribution, and the term of existence if not perpetual. Every founding member must appear personally or through a notarized power of attorney to sign the instrument. The notary must certify the acts of formation and issue a notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Certificate of personal seal impression of each member
Draft Articles of Incorporation on stamped paper
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to acknowledge the Articles because a provision violates the Commercial Act, counsel will revise the offending clause and then resubmit the signed instrument; no new government fee should arise.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Capital Deposit into Blocked Corporate Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean commercial bank (for example, Shinhan Bank, Industrial Bank of Korea, or Hana Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative organizer will open a temporary blocked corporate account at a licensed Korean commercial bank under the name of the company being formed. The founding members must transfer at least their fully subscribed capital contribution into the account; South Korean law does not impose a mandatory minimum paid-up capital but the Articles must state the exact amount. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit evidencing the blocked funds. This certificate must be submitted with the registration application and cannot be released until the court registry confirms the company registration and the corporate bank account is activated.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation and name reservation certificate
Certificate of deposit issued by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit certificate is suspended by the bank, the organizer must correct any deficiencies in beneficial ownership information under anti-money laundering verification and reissue the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registry Filing for Company Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Registration Section of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, or the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the sealed registration application to the company registration section of the local branch of the Korean District Court together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital deposit certificate, the statutory forms executed by all directors, a copy of the identification or passport of each director and member, and proof of payment of the registration tax. The court registration team will examine the instrument for formal legality against the Commercial Act and upon approval will assign a corporate registry number (Beohbeonge). The completion of registration legally creates the entity and the operator must thereafter obtain the business license.
required_dossiers: Personal identification documents of directors and members
Certificate of personal seal impression of each director
Power of attorney to the formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The district court may request a statutory cure under Article 39 of the Commercial Act if any form or payment deficiency is detected; the formation agent will provide supplemental documents within seven days and may contest the refusal through administrative appeal to the relevant court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Administration Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local National Tax Service (NTS) Tax Office, usually the branch with jurisdiction over the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory period after court registration, the newly constituted Yuhan Hoesa must file an application for business registration with the local tax office and for value added tax registration. The authorized director must present the certified copy of incorporation, corporate seal certificate, lease agreement for the registered office, director identification documents, and the bank account details. The tax office will issue a business registration certificate with a unique business license number, which authorizes the company to collect and remit VAT, issue tax invoices, and proceed with operating permits. The entire SOP must be performed before any physical catering activity starts.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for physical registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office sees a mismatch in the registered address or director information, the company shall correct the registration first at the district court and then resubmit the business registration request.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Incheon International Airport Corporation (IIAC) Commercial Affairs Department and the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) Regional Office for the Incheon/Gyeonggi Region
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Airport In-Flight Catering Facility Operating License (HACCP-certified Food Manufacturing Business License) and Airside Ramp Catering Delivery Permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and Korea Environment Corporation (K-eco)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Facilities with daily wastewater discharge below 75 cubic meters require an Environmental Registration and an Environmental Compliance Report under the Environmental Impact Assessment Decree; facilities discharging 75 cubic meters or more per day, or treating hazardous food waste streams, are classified as 'Full EIA Report / Small Environmental Impact Statement' and must obtain pre-authorization before construction
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to municipal sewers must meet BOD/COD levels of 70 mg/L or less and total suspended solids of 70 mg/L or less; oil and grease must be below 5 mg/L; kitchen exhaust volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions are limited to 10 ppm or less at stack or duct release points; hazardous waste storage must be labeled and logged under the Waste Control Act with zero release outside approved treatment facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory fire safety certificate from the local fire station under the Fire Services Act; structural load inspection and occupancy certification by the competent municipal building authority; workplace safety and health approval from KOSHA (Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency), including hygiene licensing, ventilation clearances, and food preparation worker medical certificates. High-risk kitchen operations must secure a Civil Defense inspection for refrigerant gas, fire suppression systems, and emergency egress routes.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax Service (Hometax) at https://www.hometax.go.kr; export and import clearance support is handled by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS portal at https://unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) After incorporating the Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act, the entity, or its foreign non-resident parent, must apply for statutory business registration with the district tax office of the NTS that has jurisdiction over the registered head office. 2) The application must be accompanied by the company's articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, foreign company registration extracts if applicable, personal identification of the representative director, and, if no physical Korean office is yet established, a power of attorney appointing a domestic fiscal representative for NTS procedure. 3) The NTS verifies the corporate existence and then issues a Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit Business Registration Number; that same number is the VAT registration number and functions as the legal TIN for corporate tax, e-Tax Invoices, customs export declarations, and foreign-exchange reporting. 4) To carry on export business, the Yuhan Hoesa must additionally complete the foreign trade business registration with the Korea Customs Service in UNI-PASS, using the NTS Business Registration Number as the underlying identifier for the customs exporter ID. 5) For non-resident entities without a Korean business presence that are nonetheless making taxable supplies in Korea, the NTS will accept registration through a designated tax representative; the issued Business Registration Number remains the sole VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity classification election; a Yuhan Hoesa is by law a taxable Korean corporation. Consolidated corporate tax filing is separately available to a domestic parent holding 100% of Korean subsidiaries upon an active election under the Corporate Tax Act, but it does not alter the default entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea (Korean VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None for corporations: a Yuhan Hoesa must register for VAT from its first taxable supply. The KRW 80,000,000 annual taxable turnover threshold only determines eligibility for simplified taxable person status of individual sole proprietors, and does not exempt a company from standard VAT registration and e-invoicing obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The e-Tax Invoice (electronic tax invoice) is mandatory for every taxable supply of goods or services made by the Yuhan Hoesa. The invoice must be transmitted electronically to the NTS HomeTax system, or through an NTS-integrated ERP/electronic invoice service provider via NTS Open API or certified ASP channels, no later than the close of the day following the supply date. Korea does not employ hardware-based real-time transaction clearance or digital stamping in the sense used in some EU countries; instead, the NTS administers online integrity controls for e-Tax Invoices, including a certified corporate certificate, unique sequential invoice numbers, NTS certification and a machine-readable QR code on printed representations. Invoice data is matched centrally against VAT returns, cash receipts, and customs export data for anti-fraud purposes. E-invoices are also mandatory for zero-rated export sales, and the Yuhan Hoesa must issue and transmit the zero-rated e-Tax Invoice without any paper-only exception.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Korean VAT law, goods supplied for export to foreign countries and certain services rendered overseas are zero-rated. For airport bonded in-flight catering, the following criteria must be met to claim 0% VAT: (i) the meals are manufactured in an airport bonded catering production facility or licensed airport supply area; (ii) the meals are physically delivered onto and uplifted by an aircraft operating an international route from Korea; (iii) an aircraft stores/catering manifest or equivalent flight document proves the quantity and destination; (iv) a zero-rated e-Tax Invoice is issued to the airline or its local agent; and (v) the export proceeds are received in foreign currency in Korea within 180 days from the export declaration/customs clearance. Qualifying offshore digital services supplied by the entity to non-resident customers would also be zero-rated when consumed outside Korea, but any B2B digital services supplied to a Korean VAT-registered recipient remain taxable at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Clearance Certificate) filed with and accepted by the Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS, identifying the catering supplies as export, bonded uplift or aircraft stores shipment

Air Waybill, export cargo manifest, or international aircraft stores list, including a signed catering uplift/loading manifest from the airline or ground handling agent evidencing that the in-flight meals were loaded onto the specified international flight

Foreign Exchange Repatriation Certificate or Foreign Exchange Purchase Certificate (foreign currency purchase confirmation) issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, evidencing receipt of export proceeds within the 180-day period, or an approved netting/settlement certificate where application is accepted
Zero-rated e-Tax Invoice bearing the Yuhan Hoesa VAT registration number and the 0% zero-rated code, together with its NTS transmission acceptance record
Sales agreement or airline purchase order with the non-Korean airline or its approved ground handling subsidiary, and the payment rail confirmation (aviation contract wire or monthly ACH)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service will cross-check export declarations, aircraft departure status, load/catering manifests, e-Tax Invoices, and banking import/export proceeds records. If the exporter cannot provide a complete statutory file proving physical export and foreign-exchange repatriation, the 0% rate is reversed and the supply is recharacterised as domestic taxable supply: the Yuhan Hoesa must then pay 10% VAT, plus statutory overdue interest and additional tax under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes, including daily late-payment additional tax and short-reporting additions for negligent understatement. Any VAT refund paid on the basis of the disallowed zero-rating is clawed back together with interest. A false or sham export, forged customs export documents, or non-repatriated export proceeds beyond 180 days without an approved extension may expose the entity and responsible officers to criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, including imprisonment and fines calculated on the tax evaded or the amount of foreign exchange withheld.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and delegated authority from the Korean Ministry of Economy and Finance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea operates a fundamentally liberalised current-account regime, permitting routine foreign exchange transactions for trade, services, dividends, and royalties with minimal administrative friction. For airline in-flight catering services, Korean-registered legal entities may receive cross-border wire transfers through domestic banks under standard receipt notifications to the designated foreign exchange bank. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA), current account transactions are freely permitted, while capital account transactions such as direct equity investment, loans, and securities transactions require statutory declaration or reporting through banks. A foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa must file a Foreign Investment Report with KOTRA or a delegated domestic bank before inbound capital can be wired. Profit remittance in the form of dividends is permitted on an annual basis once audited financial statements are adopted, but the remittance will trigger dividend withholding tax at 22% absent treaty reduction, and banks will require proof of the foreign investment report, tax clearance, and board resolutions. Korea does not impose a compulsory conversion of export proceeds into KRW, but export proceeds must be collected within the statutory inward collection period of six months from shipment unless an exemption is granted. The Won is freely convertible; however, banks must report suspicious cross-border flows and aggregate FX transactions to the Bank of Korea and Korea Customs Service. This is therefore an open but dokumentarily rigorous regime for treasury operations, and no exchange-certificate approval is needed for standard aviation catering contracts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from the in-flight catering business must be received within six months from the date of shipment under FETA Article 14 and related Bank of Korea regulations. There is no mandatory minimum conversion ratio; export receipts may be retained in foreign currency or converted to KRW at the exporter's discretion. Inward collection extensions require a documented application to the designated foreign exchange bank, typically with airline payment terms, reason for delay, and revised settlement schedule. Exporters must report the inward receipt to the designated bank or customs within the prescribed timeline, and failure to collect within six months without authorisation can trigger administrative penalties and possible foreign exchange offence review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational KRW and USD Currency Accounts
Basic Operational KRW Currency Account / Export Proceeds Receivable Foreign Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Trade Settlement Foreign Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Payroll and Domestic Disbursement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Pure offshore fintech EMIs and digital-challenger payment service providers are not viable as primary operating banks for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa. Korean banking law reserves domestic foreign-currency account opening and Foreign Investment Report handling to licensed banking institutions. Internet-only banks such as KakaoBank and Toss Bank may provide KRW accounts to domestic corporations, but their appetite and operational readiness for foreign-invested companies with cross-border aviation receivables is moderate at best, and they do not offer the full array of trade finance instruments, MT103 processing, or foreign exchange hedging desks required for airline catering operations. Offshore non-bank EMI entities such as Wise, Revolut Business, and Airwallex cannot provide a compliant Korean settlement account or act as the designated foreign exchange bank for FETA reporting. They may be used only as auxiliary collections channels where a licensed Korean bank is used as the treasury anchor, and even then the treasurer should be aware that Korean beneficiary account details will not include offshore EMI IBANs. The prudent blueprint is to rely exclusively on a top-tier Korean commercial bank as the settlement anchor and treat any fintech EMI as a dismissed option.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch physical presence is the default requirement during the account opening interview for a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa. Statutory directors or the authorised senior treasury officer are generally required to appear in person at the main branch of the designated foreign exchange bank to execute the corporate account opening forms, certify the corporate seal, and undergo an in-person identification interview under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act. A remote consular proxy opening is not universally accepted because Korean banks typically require the actual corporate representative's passport, alien registration card or proof of residence, and a live verification of the legal representative's identity. In exceptional cases, a corporate director may execute a notarised and apostilled power of attorney in favour of a resident Korean finance manager, and the bank may then permit the resident attorney-in-fact to attend the physical interview bearing the original apostilled documents. However, most Korean banks will still perform a video-call confirmation with the statutory director before the account is activated. The safest onboarding plan is to schedule a non-resident director's visit to Seoul for one or two banking days, with all corporate registration documents pre-translated and apostilled, and to assign a local resident financial officer as a co-signatory to minimise future physical attendance needs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained beneficial ownership chain with foreign shareholders hiding behind an intermediate offshore entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full corporate ownership chart from the final individual human beneficial owner to the Korean Yuhan Hoesa, showing each intermediate entity's jurisdiction, registration number, and constitutional documents. This must be supported by audited financial statements of the ultimate shareholder, a sworn beneficial ownership declaration, passport copies of the ultimate beneficial owner with legalisation, and internationally accepted background checks or sanctions screening results from a reputable screening provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or potential PEP status of a Korean statutory director or ultimate shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A personal bank reference letter from a Tier-1 financial institution in the director's domicile, a comprehensive CV or business biography, extraction from national corporate registry showing other legitimate board positions, and a formal written declaration of politically exposed person status with detailed source-of-wealth documentation including salary contracts, real estate registration extracts, stock sales records, and tax statements covering the last five years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected invoice manipulation or false trade because the entity is an in-flight caterer with complex structured contracts connecting the airline, ground handler, and kitchen operator.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master in-flight catering agreements with the airline counterparty, flight schedule documentation or service orders for each route, detailed invoices and goods-delivery notes reconciled to the airline's online portal, and a standard cost breakdown for raw food materials, kitchen labour, portion packaging, and ramp transport. The compliance committee will also expect a copy of the public aviation catering license, food sanitation certificate, and customs operating matrix for the airport bonded area.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume third-party payments from regional travel facilitators or aviation agents that create a commingled and unclear payment routing pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury policy document naming all approved counterparties with relationship declarations, written confirmation from the airline that all catering settlements are directed from its treasury department or its authorised subsidiary list, a sample archive of ten reconciliations between SWIFT payment confirmations and invoiced flight schedules, and a signed memorandum of understanding with the Korean bank providing visibility into the contracting hierarchy of every inbound credit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must be routed through a designated foreign exchange bank in Korea. Before funds are wired, the foreign investor must submit a foreign-investment report to KOTRA or a delegated bank branch, specifying the total investment amount, shareholding percentage, and intended business scope. After report acceptance, the investor opens a temporary foreign currency receipt account under an escrow arrangement or a dedicated capital account with the Korean bank, and the overseas bank remits the equity contribution via a SWIFT MT103, referencing the foreign-investment report number. The Korean bank will verify the incoming funds, attribute them to the capital account under the Capital Account Liberalisation framework, and issue a Certificate of Foreign Capital Investment, which is essential for subsequent dividend remittances, repatriation of capital, and legal review by the Ministry of Economy and Finance. The funds must remain son the dedicated account until the corporate registration and Korean FDI notification procedures are complete; once documented, the funds may be transferred into the operating KRW account and used for licensed business expenditures. All post-transaction foreign exchange statements must be archived to satisfy potential audits by the National Tax Service and the Bank of Korea.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade-related disbursements, the Korean Yuhan Hoesa will use its designated foreign exchange bank to execute SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for low-value transaction payments and recurring annuity-style payments to overseas raw material suppliers. For high-value or documentary trade settlements, the bank will issue Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits) to the foreign seller, with terms requiring presentation of the air waybill, invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, and phytosanitary certificates for inbound food ingredients. For open-account settlements with established overseas suppliers, the treasury can utilise documentary collections (D/P and D/A) through the Korean bank's correspondent banking network, though the airline's monthly settlement cycle is more efficiently handled via clean MT103 remittances tied to the monthly ACH reconciliation of meal counts. Domestic treasury obligations, such as kitchen payroll, airport ground handling fees, and refrigeration bills, should settle through the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute (KFTC) retail or corporate ACH rails, with the appropriate corporate business day cut-off. The bank will require a written instruction authorising the use of the specific purpose code for each outward payment, especially for food procurement, freight, royalties, and related services, to ensure alignment with FETA reporting requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_insur_instruments: Forward exchange contracts with the designated foreign exchange bank for USD/KRW and commonly traded G10 currency pairs, available up to one year with physical delivery and tied to commercial invoices for catering food imports and airline settlement receivables.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) arrangements are generally permissible for Korean residents only in limited offshore arbitrage or exceptional margin-protection scenarios; such contracts are usually executed through on-shore bank relationships under strict commercial rationale documentation, and the bank will require evidence of underlying trade exposure.

Cross-currency swaps between USD and KRW are permissible for long-term balance-sheet prudential management, but must be clearly linked to outstanding foreign shareholder loans, bond issuance, or long-term supply contracts, and will require board approval plus a confirmed hedge accounting designation.

Vanilla FX option strategies such as purchased call options are permissible under Korean FX regulations; however, the entity must present detailed board minutes and the hedge must be documented under the bank's FX sales policy to preserve FETA compliance and avoid treatment as a speculative derivative.

stage_4._financial_reality_check_placeholder: This blueprint is based strictly on the Korean Financial Investment Services, Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and Bank of Korea operational standards as of the current review date; no fintech EMI is recommended for the core treasury mandate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Juridical Person Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - Seoul Regional Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months from fiscal year end (March 31 for calendar-year companies); extension to April 30 allowed upon prior application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underreporting penalty of 20% (40% for fraudulent omission) of evaded tax plus daily late-payment interest of 0.022% (approx. 8.03% annual); repeated non-filing can lead to business registration cancellation, compulsory collection, and court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - assigned district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half: July 25; second half: January 25 (calendar-year basis); online filing grants automatic 1-month extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty 10% to 20% of unpaid VAT (up to 30% for fraudulent omission); daily late-payment interest 0.022%; persistent non-filing triggers business closure and criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surtax on Corporate Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: City or Province where the registered office is located (e.g., Seoul Metropolitan Government)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as corporate income tax return (March 31/April 30 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment charge of 3% plus daily interest 0.022%; enforced seizure of assets; administrative closure or revocation of business registration for habitual default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Wage Report and Labor Insurance Contribution Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Employment Information Service; National Pension Service; National Health Insurance Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By February 15 of the year following the wage payment year (for preceding calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative surcharge up to 10% of unpaid premiums; criminal fines up to KRW 50 million for willful non-report; delinquency may also trigger civil penalties and labor inspection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements (mandatory only where statutory threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the court with jurisdiction over the company's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year end (June 30 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to undergo external audit triggers administrative fine up to KRW 30 million, criminal liability for directors, and possible court dissolution order for acute non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Members' Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal members' resolution; minutes and financial statements retained at the registered office and available to the NTS upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the fiscal year (by June 30 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No administrative fine on its own, but failure to hold AGM invalidates dividend distribution, exposes directors to civil liability, and may be cited in tax audits as cause for re-assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Food Manufacturing Business Report / Annual Hygiene Self-Assessment (airline inflight catering)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) - regional office in cooperation with Incheon Airport authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the license anniversary date or by March 31 depending on the original business report registration; any material change must be re-reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate operational shutdown order; administrative fine up to KRW 10 million; suspension or revocation of the food business license for serious or repeat violations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies etc. (effective FY 2023), a mandatory independent certified CPA audit is required if any of the following conditions are met: (i) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 8.6 million) at the fiscal year-end; (ii) the entity is listed on a Korean stock exchange; (iii) the entity conducts banking, insurance, securities, or other specified financial activities regardless of asset size; or (iv) the entity is designated by the Financial Supervisory Service as being in a high-risk or public-interest category. For a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) with only airline inflight catering operations, the quantitative size test under (i) and any FSS designation trigger are the relevant criteria.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for listed companies and financial institutions; privately held SMEs and LLCs may apply K-IFRS on a voluntary basis or adopt Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) as approved by the Korean Accounting Standards Board, including the simplified Level 3 standards for small private companies. Audited entities must present financial statements in compliance with either K-IFRS or K-GAAP consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not require a separate annual UBO confirmation filing for a private Yuhan Hoesa (LLC). However, under the Commercial Act, any change of members (shareholders) or registered officers must be filed with the Korean registry court (Company Registration Office) within 14 days of the change, and the share transfer is effective only when recorded in the company's members' register. For capital gains tax purposes, the transferor of non-listed shares must file the transferor's tax return to the NTS within one month following the end of the calendar quarter in which the transfer occurred (Q4 transfers by January 31), which is effectively a 30-day reporting window. In addition, companies subject to external audit must disclose the ultimate beneficial owner in audit workpapers, but no dedicated annual UBO filing is made to any Korean regulator.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 1,500 per year for a compliant registered office/agent address in Seoul, with higher tiers including meeting room access or business support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 15,000 per year, equivalent to KRW 4,000,000 - 20,000,000, depending on transaction volume, number of subsidiaries, and complexity of the inflight catering operation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national top marginal CIT rate (progressive brackets: 9% up to KRW 200m, 19% up to KRW 20bn, 21% up to KRW 300bn, 24% over KRW 300bn) plus 10% local income tax surtax, yielding a combined top effective rate of 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket tax holiday; possible incentives include Free Economic Zone preferential tax deferral under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (RSTA), foreign-invested enterprise income tax reductions, R&D tax credits up to 30% for qualifying activities, and investment tax credits for airport logistics automation; local surtax may be reduced in certain provinces.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (the standard domestic corporation return) filed with the National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing system (hometax.go.kr), including the International Transactions Reporting Schedule and the Tax Treaty Relief Attachment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with a mandatory semi-annual interim prepayment declaration for companies with recurring income).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed by the end of the third month following the fiscal year-end (e.g., a December 31 year-end filing deadline is March 31); the interim prepayment return is due within two months after the end of the first six months of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Entity Identification and Foreign Non-Resident Ownership Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the Yuhan Hoesa and lists all non-resident shareholders, their countries of residence, equity percentages, and whether a tax treaty claim is made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident shareholder, attach the Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), a beneficial ownership statement, and the Foreign Investment Notice if capital exceeds KRW 100 million. A treaty relief application must be filed if reduced withholding is intended. Omission of a 1% or larger foreign holding triggers a penalty of 10% of the understated tax and may invalidate DTA benefits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Related-Party International Transaction Schedule (Local File / Master File Trigger)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares every cross-border intercompany transaction: catering sales to airline affiliates, dry-ice supply chain, royalty fees, management charges, and financial costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If annual international intercompany transactions exceed KRW 5 billion, the Local File and Master File must be submitted together with this box; otherwise, an attached statement must state that the threshold is not met. Use OECD transfer pricing methods and keep time-series data. Failure to complete this schedule is treated as an intentional misleading return, enabling the NTS to adjust income and impose a 10% transfer pricing penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Foreign Tax Credit and Domestic-Source Income Reallocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes taxes paid to a foreign country that may be credited against Korean CIT, and reconciles any income attributable to foreign permanent establishments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: In a non-resident-owned catering company, review whether overseas kitchen purchase commissions or airline base charges actually constitute foreign income. Only external taxes legally owed and paid abroad are credit-eligible; mismatched timing requires carryforward/carryback application. Provide the Foreign Tax Credit Computation worksheet; missing documentation causes disallowance of the credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 17 - Withholding Tax on Payments to Non-Residents (Dividends, Interest, Royalties, Service Fees)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reports gross amounts paid or credited to foreign shareholders/contractors and applies withholding tax at statutory or treaty-reduced rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For any outbound dividend, interest, rental of kitchen equipment, or franchise royalty, apply the 22% statutory rate (20% national plus 2% local surtax) unless a treaty reduction was approved in advance. To claim a reduction, the beneficiary must have filed an NTS Treaty Reduction Application with TRC and substance evidence before remittance. The payer is the withholding agent; failing to withhold makes the director personally liable for the amount plus penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file: negligence tax of 10% of the unpaid tax, with a minimum of KRW 100,000; an additional daily penalty of 0.03% on overdue tax; false declaration: 20% of the under-reported amount; unfaithful schedule reporting: 5% penalty; tax fraud exceeding KRW 300 million adds criminal fines up to 3 times the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years. Directors who commit willful omission face travel bans, asset seizures, and personal liability for the corporate debt.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax) for dividends paid to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain reduced rates under a Double Tax Treaty, the non-resident beneficiary must (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the home-country tax authority within the last 12 months; (ii) execute a Korean treaty-relief declaration form and file it with the NTS before or at the time of the first payment; (iii) submit a beneficial ownership certificate evidencing the right to the income, the absence of a pass-through arrangement, and the existence of economic substance (employees, premises, bank account); and (iv) attach a copy of the applicable treaty article. The NTS may require an advance ruling through the 'Tax Treaty Reduction/Exemption Application' procedure. Without this filing, the full 22% is withheld; a refund may be claimed within 3 years, but with practical risks of interest and audit scrutiny.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates for outbound interest and royalties are 22% (20% national plus 2% local surtax). Under Korea's treaty network, interest is typically reduced to 10%, royalties to 10%–15% depending on the treaty and the character of the IP, and dividends to 5%–15%, always subject to limitation-of-benefits and beneficial-ownership checks.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: While Korea does not have a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) filing analogous to the UAE, the substance-over-form doctrine is embedded in the Corporate Income Tax Act and the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LICAA). An inflight catering entity must demonstrate actual decision-making, procurement, production, and ramp delivery in Korea through active employees, physical kitchen facilities, and airline contracts. Where a shell vehicle is used only to hold treaty benefits and bonded customs privileges, the NTS will disregard the vehicle, reallocate profits to the real taxpayer, and apply CFC rules to penalize offshore passive income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or receiving false inflight catering invoices, concealing sales to airline affiliates, overstating food rejection and wastage costs, or fabricating kitchen-worker payroll in order to artificially reduce the Korean taxable income of the Yuhan Hoesa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, Article 3, the company is liable for a fine up to 3 times the evaded tax, plus administrative negligence tax of 20%–40% of the unreported amount; the NTS may additionally revoke the bonded warehouse license under the Customs Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced because the tax offense is committed through deliberate acts of the directors. They become jointly and severally liable for the assessed taxes and fines, and may be subject to asset seizure, entry refusal (travel blacklist) if the evaded tax exceeds KRW 300 million, and criminal imprisonment up to 5 years. All directors of a Korean LLC are personally accountable for intentional tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation / Offshore Profit Leakage
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying large 'management' or 'royalty' fees to a related non-resident entity with no real office, employees or IP, or selling cooling and catering equipment to an offshore affiliate at below-market value; alternatively, failing to prepare contemporaneous Local File/Master File when annual intercompany transactions with a foreign related party exceed KRW 5 billion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LICAA), Articles 4 and 5, the NTS adjusts taxable income to the arm's length price, imposes a 10% penalty on the understated income, and levies a KRW 50 million fine for material documentation failure; treaty mutual agreement procedure relief is denied for transactions tainted by intentional manipulation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized non-arm's length pricing are personally responsible for the adjusted tax, additions, and penalties if the corporate entity cannot pay; their participation constitutes joint tortious conduct under the Commercial Act. They may be blacklisted from leaving Korea, their Korean bank accounts may be frozen, and each director can face up to 5 years' imprisonment for deliberate false reporting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse / Treaty Shopping and AML-Connected Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Yuhan Hoesa as a letterbox entity with no real catering staff, kitchen operations, or airport ramp vehicles; using it solely to channel foreign investment and claim tax treaty benefits, duty-free fuel/food imports, and free-trade-zone incentives; or commingling catering receipts with illegal proceeds in a manner that triggers Korean AML obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Offenses, Article 3, sanctions embezzlement/misappropriation with imprisonment up to life for extremely high amounts; the Customs Act allows import duty evasion penalties up to 10 times the evaded duties and seizure of imported kitchen equipment; the Financial Transactions Report Act and AML regulations impose administrative fines up to KRW 100 million per violation and criminal sanctions up to 5 years for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The lack of substance is used to pierce the corporate veil under Korean Supreme Court precedent: the director's personal assets and overseas assets traceable to the shell structure are subject to civil restitution. The director is placed on the financial blacklist, receives a travel ban, and can be imprisoned up to 7 years. If the shell is used to evade foreign taxes on income diverted from Korea, extradition procedures may also be initiated.
